subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: What should OpenClaw do when a configured provider emits only a bare allowed-tool marker such as `[tool: exec]` with no arguments and no structured tool call?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe behavior is a product/runtime policy choice because direct execution lacks arguments and fallback, retry, warning, or model restriction each affects provider compatibility differently.

options.title: Warn or fail over without executing
options.body: Classify the bare marker as tool-capability failure, notify or fall through to a tool-capable model, and execute only repaired calls with explicit arguments.

options.title: Retry with stricter tool guidance
options.body: Retry the turn once with provider-specific guidance or forced tool choice, accepting extra latency and possible repeated failure for weaker compatibility routes.

options.title: Promote bare markers to empty calls
options.body: Convert known markers into zero-argument tool calls, which may unblock some tools but risks unsafe or misleading execution for tools that require arguments.

recommendation.title: Warn or fail over without executing
recommendation.body: Classify the bare marker as tool-capability failure, notify or fall through to a tool-capable model, and execute only repaired calls with explicit arguments.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the provider stream SDK/runtime boundary where recent ownership history is strongest.
